This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

1	"""Shared SQL-datasource primitives: the identifier allowlist (#428), the
2	lazy engine lifecycle (#427), and the statement-echo strip (#1203).
3	
4	SQL identifiers have no bind-parameter slot, so every path that interpolates a
5	user-supplied table/schema/column into a query string (monitor config, the
6	profiler's query builders) validates against this one decision first — widening
7	it (e.g. quoted/unicode identifiers) then happens everywhere at once. Callers
8	keep their own error types; the shared piece is the decision, not the failure
9	shape.
10	
11	`LazyEngine` is the one build-once/dispose-once engine holder the SQL runners
12	(Snowflake / Unity Catalog) share — only the URL/connect-args factory varies per
13	runner, so lifecycle fixes (pre-ping, dispose semantics, guards) land in one
14	place instead of drifting between copies. No import cycle: this module knows
15	nothing about monitors or runners.
16	
17	`strip_statement_echo` lives here for the same reason: the tail SQLAlchemy
18	appends to a failed statement is a property of the SQL engine, not of any one
19	datasource, so Snowflake and Unity Catalog (and any future SQL type) get the
20	identical treatment from one implementation.
21	"""
22	
23	from __future__ import annotations
24	
25	import re
26	from collections.abc import Callable
27	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Final
28	
29	if TYPE_CHECKING:
30	    from sqlalchemy.engine.interfaces import Dialect
31	    from sqlalchemy.sql import TableClause
32	
33	# The Snowflake/Databricks unquoted-identifier set: letter/underscore lead, then
34	# word chars or `$`. Private — go through `is_sql_identifier`, whose isinstance
35	# guard keeps a non-string config value (JSON ints/lists/None) a clean rejection
36	# instead of a re TypeError at the match call.
37	_SQL_IDENTIFIER_RE: Final = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*")
38	
39	
40	def is_sql_identifier(name: object) -> bool:
41	    """True when ``name`` is a plain SQL identifier safe to interpolate.
42	
43	    Anything else (spaces, quotes, dots, a trailing newline, non-strings) is
44	    refused — it can't be made injection-safe by quoting alone at the call sites
45	    that use this. ``fullmatch``, not ``match`` + ``$``: the ``$`` anchor accepts
46	    one trailing ``\\n``, which has no business in an identifier.
47	    """
48	    return isinstance(name, str) and bool(_SQL_IDENTIFIER_RE.fullmatch(name))
49	
50	
51	# Where `sqlalchemy.exc.StatementError._sql_message` stops reporting the error and
52	# starts echoing `.statement` / `.params`. Its rendering is fixed:
53	#
54	#     (snowflake.connector.errors.ProgrammingError) 100038 (22018): Numeric value
55	#     'ORD-9-not-a-number' is not recognized
56	#     [SQL: SELECT ... WHERE customer_ref = %(ref)s]
57	#     [parameters: {'ref': 'a@example.com'}]
58	#     (Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/20/f405)
59	#
60	# — the driver's own message first, then `"[SQL: %s]" % self.statement`, then
61	# `"[parameters: %r]"` (only ever emitted when the statement was), then the doc
62	# link, joined with newlines. So the marker is SQLAlchemy's own delimiter between
63	# "what went wrong" and "here is the query and its bound values": cutting at it is
64	# a structural split of a known rendering, NOT a heuristic over the prose.
65	_STATEMENT_ECHO_MARKER: Final = "\n[SQL: "
66	
67	
68	def strip_statement_echo(message: str | None) -> str | None:
69	    """Drop the ``[SQL: …] [parameters: …]`` tail SQLAlchemy appends to a failed
70	    statement, keeping the driver's own message (#1203).
71	
72	    The bound parameters are **target data**: they are the cell values DataQ sent
73	    back to the warehouse, and they land in ``results.observed_value``, which is
74	    outside the `sample_failures` retention sweep and outside the suite's column
75	    redaction policy — so from there they reach the run-detail API, the UI, alerts
76	    and MCP output unmasked. The statement itself can echo the same values inline
77	    (a literal in a custom-SQL check). Neither belongs in a persisted, broadly
78	    readable field.
79	
80	    What is deliberately KEPT is the driver's own first block. That message is the
81	    most actionable thing a user gets for a broken query ("Numeric value 'x' is not
82	    recognized", "Table does not exist"), and blanket-classifying it the way
83	    `failure_classifier` treats a connect failure would make a bad cast or a typo'd
84	    column undiagnosable from the UI — the same trade-off `SafeMonitorError`'s
85	    docstring records for `MonitorConfigError`. A warehouse message can quote the
86	    offending cell, and that is accepted here: it is the diagnostic, it is bounded
87	    to one value the driver chose to name, and removing it would leave the user
88	    with nothing. What this closes is the *bulk*, mechanical echo of the statement
89	    and every bound parameter, which is neither bounded nor diagnostic — the query
90	    is already visible to its author in the check editor.
91	
92	    Idempotent, and a no-op on any message without the marker (a non-SQL engine's
93	    exception, a DataQ-authored message, ``None``), so it is safe to apply both
94	    where the message is persisted and where it is read back.
95	    """
96	    if not message:
97	        return message
98	    head, marker, _ = message.partition(_STATEMENT_ECHO_MARKER)
99	    return head.rstrip() if marker else message
100	
101	
102	def folding_identifier(name: str) -> Any:
103	    """Wrap ``name`` with an explicit quote decision: bare iff it is all lower-case.
104	
105	    The #476 rule, made ours instead of SQLAlchemy's. Left to its defaults the
106	    compiler also quotes any name in the **dialect's reserved-word set**, which is
107	    not the same set the warehouse reserves — Snowflake does not reserve ``copy``,
108	    but SQLAlchemy's Snowflake dialect does, so a column stored ``COPY`` (created
109	    unquoted as ``copy``) would be emitted as ``"copy"`` and stop resolving. That
110	    is the very failure #476 exists to remove, reintroduced for one word.
111	
112	    Pinning the decision explicitly makes the emitted form depend only on case:
113	
114	    * **all lower-case → never quoted**, so the warehouse folds it exactly as it
115	      did before #476 (``order_ts`` → ``ORDER_TS``). This is what makes the change
116	      byte-for-byte behaviour-preserving rather than approximately so.
117	    * **anything else → always quoted**, which is the whole point: a mixed-case
118	      column is only reachable quoted.
119	
120	    Genuinely reserved words (``order``, ``select``) are unreachable either way —
121	    bare is a parse error, and the folded object is ``ORDER``, which ``"order"``
122	    does not match. They were broken before this change and are broken after it,
123	    identically; alias them in a view.
124	    """
125	    from sqlalchemy.sql import quoted_name
126	
127	    return quoted_name(name, quote=name != name.lower())
128	
129	
130	def _quote_namespace_part(name: str, dialect: Dialect) -> str:
131	    """Apply `folding_identifier`'s case-based decision to one namespace part
132	    that is about to be hand-assembled into a pre-quoted, dotted string (the
133	    3-part ``catalog.schema`` case — see `core_table`).
134	
135	    A plain ``quoted_name`` can't be used here: Core's own quoting decision
136	    (`IdentifierPreparer.quote`) also fires on the dialect's *reserved-word*
137	    set, which is exactly what `folding_identifier` exists to bypass (#476).
138	    So the "should I quote" call is made here, case-only, same as
139	    `folding_identifier`; only the actual wrapping — the quote *character* —
140	    is delegated to the dialect, via ``identifier_preparer.quote_identifier``,
141	    which just wraps + escapes and makes no quoting decision of its own.
142	    """
143	    if name == name.lower():
144	        return name
145	    return str(dialect.identifier_preparer.quote_identifier(name))
146	
147	
148	def core_table(
149	    *,
150	    table: str,
151	    schema: str | None,
152	    catalog: str | None,
153	    dialect: Dialect | None = None,
154	) -> TableClause:
155	    """A Core table clause for ``[catalog.][schema.]table`` — the dialect quotes it.
156	
157	    The one construction shared by the profiler's query builders and the monitor
158	    engine (#476). Going through Core rather than f-string interpolation is what
159	    makes a **mixed-case identifier** work at all, per `folding_identifier`'s rule.
160	
161	    It must be Core and not hand-rolled quoting because the quote character is
162	    **dialect-specific** — Snowflake uses ``"``, Databricks/Unity Catalog uses
163	    backticks and reads ``"..."`` as a string literal — and this module is shared
164	    by both.
165	
166	    **The 3-part (catalog) form needs a live ``dialect`` (#936).** Core's
167	    ``schema=`` slot is a single string, so a ``catalog.schema.table`` namespace
168	    has to be pre-assembled as one string for the dialect to emit dotted parts
169	    rather than quoting the whole thing as one identifier — and getting each part
170	    individually quote-correct then means making the "should I quote" decision
171	    ourselves (`_quote_namespace_part`, `folding_identifier`'s case rule applied
172	    per part) and, when a part needs quoting, wrapping it with the **dialect's
173	    own** ``identifier_preparer.quote_identifier`` rather than a hardcoded ``"``
174	    or backtick — so Snowflake and Unity Catalog each still get their own quote
175	    character despite the hand-assembly.
176	
177	    All **three** parts go through the pre-assembly, not just catalog/schema —
178	    including the table, and via ``schema=None`` rather than Core's ``schema=``
179	    slot. Snowflake's own SQLAlchemy dialect turns out to already special-case a
180	    dotted *schema* string: ``quote_schema`` re-**splits** it back into parts and
181	    re-derives each part's quote decision from the whole string's single
182	    ``.quote`` flag, discarding any quote characters embedded in the parts
183	    themselves — so a schema-slot ``"MyCat"."Retail"`` (quote=False) round-trips
184	    back out as the *unquoted* ``MyCat.Retail``, silently undoing this fix on the
185	    one dialect it exists for. The **table**-name slot has no such override
186	    (``format_table``'s own name is quoted with the plain, non-splitting
187	    ``IdentifierPreparer.quote``), so folding the whole pre-quoted namespace in
188	    there — table included — and leaving ``schema=None`` sidesteps the
189	    reinterpretation entirely, on every dialect tested (Snowflake, Databricks,
190	    the SQLAlchemy default).
191	
192	    A ``catalog`` with no ``dialect`` is a caller bug (every production caller has
193	    one available — the runner's engine, or the profiler/anomaly path's open
194	    connection) and is raised as `ValueError` rather than silently under-quoting
195	    again.
196	
197	    That pre-quoted namespace is also the one raw interpolation left in the
198	    module, hence the allowlist check on every part here rather than trusting
199	    callers (they validate first for a good error message; this is the injection
200	    guarantee, and it survives a caller forgetting to validate).
201	
202	    A ``catalog`` with no ``schema`` is refused: dropping the ``None`` schema would
203	    emit a 2-part ``catalog.table``, which Unity Catalog resolves as
204	    ``schema.table`` — a wrong object rather than an error.
205	    """
206	    from sqlalchemy import table as table_clause
207	    from sqlalchemy.sql import quoted_name
208	
209	    if catalog is not None and schema is None:
210	        raise ValueError(f"table {table!r} has a catalog but no schema")
211	    for part, label in ((table, "table"), (schema, "schema"), (catalog, "catalog")):
212	        if part is not None and not is_sql_identifier(part):
213	            raise ValueError(f"invalid {label} identifier: {part!r}")
214	
215	    if catalog is not None:
216	        if dialect is None:
217	            raise ValueError(f"table {table!r} has a catalog but no dialect to quote it")
218	        assert schema is not None  # guaranteed by the catalog/schema check above
219	        full = quoted_name(
220	            ".".join(_quote_namespace_part(part, dialect) for part in (catalog, schema, table)),
221	            quote=False,
222	        )
223	        return table_clause(full, schema=None)
224	
225	    namespace: Any = None if schema is None else folding_identifier(schema)
226	    return table_clause(folding_identifier(table), schema=namespace)
227	
228	
229	def qualified_sql_name(
230	    *, table: str, schema: str | None, catalog: str | None, dialect: Dialect
231	) -> str:
232	    """``[catalog.][schema.]table`` as a pre-quoted string for a `text()` statement.
233	
234	    `core_table` is the right tool wherever a Core `Select` can express the query;
235	    this exists for the one shape Core cannot render — a dialect-specific clause
236	    that attaches to the FROM item itself, like Databricks' ``TABLESAMPLE (x
237	    PERCENT)`` (#595). It reuses `_quote_namespace_part`, so each part gets
238	    `folding_identifier`'s case-only decision and, when it needs quoting, the
239	    **dialect's own** quote character (Snowflake ``"``, Databricks backticks) —
240	    never a hardcoded one, which is what made #476's hand-rolled quoting wrong on
241	    Unity Catalog.
242	
243	    Every part is allowlist-checked here rather than trusted from the caller: this
244	    string is interpolated into SQL, so the injection guarantee has to survive a
245	    caller forgetting to validate first (the same reasoning `core_table` records).
246	    """
247	    if catalog is not None and schema is None:
248	        raise ValueError(f"table {table!r} has a catalog but no schema")
249	    parts = [(catalog, "catalog"), (schema, "schema"), (table, "table")]
250	    for part, label in parts:
251	        if part is not None and not is_sql_identifier(part):
252	            raise ValueError(f"invalid {label} identifier: {part!r}")
253	    return ".".join(_quote_namespace_part(part, dialect) for part, _ in parts if part is not None)
254	
255	
256	class LazyEngine:
257	    """One lazily-built SQLAlchemy engine with an idempotent dispose (#427).
258	
259	    ``factory`` builds the engine on first :meth:`get` (the runner's URL /
260	    connect-args closure — the only per-datasource variance); every later call
261	    returns the same engine, so a runner's SQL touchpoints share one pool and
262	    one auth handshake per run. :meth:`close` disposes the pool and resets, so
263	    a closed holder lazily rebuilds if reused — never a bricked runner.
264	    """
265	
266	    def __init__(self, factory: Callable[[], Any]) -> None:
267	        self._factory = factory
268	        self._engine: Any | None = None
269	
270	    def get(self) -> Any:
271	        if self._engine is None:
272	            self._engine = self._factory()
273	        return self._engine
274	
275	    def close(self) -> None:
276	        if self._engine is not None:
277	            self._engine.dispose()
278	            self._engine = None
279

nothing about monitors or runners.

`strip_statement_echo` lives here for the same reason: the tail SQLAlchemy
appends to a failed statement is a property of the SQL engine, not of any one
datasource, so Snowflake and Unity Catalog (and any future SQL type) get the
identical treatment from one implementation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Final

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from sqlalchemy.engine.interfaces import Dialect
    from sqlalchemy.sql import TableClause

# The Snowflake/Databricks unquoted-identifier set: letter/underscore lead, then
# word chars or `$`. Private — go through `is_sql_identifier`, whose isinstance
# guard keeps a non-string config value (JSON ints/lists/None) a clean rejection
# instead of a re TypeError at the match call.
_SQL_IDENTIFIER_RE: Final = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*")


def is_sql_identifier(name: object) -> bool:
    """True when ``name`` is a plain SQL identifier safe to interpolate.

    Anything else (spaces, quotes, dots, a trailing newline, non-strings) is
    refused — it can't be made injection-safe by quoting alone at the call sites
    that use this. ``fullmatch``, not ``match`` + ``$``: the ``$`` anchor accepts
    one trailing ``\\n``, which has no business in an identifier.
    """
    return isinstance(name, str) and bool(_SQL_IDENTIFIER_RE.fullmatch(name))


# Where `sqlalchemy.exc.StatementError._sql_message` stops reporting the error and
# starts echoing `.statement` / `.params`. Its rendering is fixed:
#
#     (snowflake.connector.errors.ProgrammingError) 100038 (22018): Numeric value
#     'ORD-9-not-a-number' is not recognized
#     [SQL: SELECT ... WHERE customer_ref = %(ref)s]
#     [parameters: {'ref': 'a@example.com'}]
#     (Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/20/f405)
#
# — the driver's own message first, then `"[SQL: %s]" % self.statement`, then
# `"[parameters: %r]"` (only ever emitted when the statement was), then the doc
# link, joined with newlines. So the marker is SQLAlchemy's own delimiter between
# "what went wrong" and "here is the query and its bound values": cutting at it is
# a structural split of a known rendering, NOT a heuristic over the prose.
_STATEMENT_ECHO_MARKER: Final = "\n[SQL: "


def strip_statement_echo(message: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Drop the ``[SQL: …] [parameters: …]`` tail SQLAlchemy appends to a failed
    statement, keeping the driver's own message (#1203).

    The bound parameters are **target data**: they are the cell values DataQ sent
    back to the warehouse, and they land in ``results.observed_value``, which is
    outside the `sample_failures` retention sweep and outside the suite's column
    redaction policy — so from there they reach the run-detail API, the UI, alerts
    and MCP output unmasked. The statement itself can echo the same values inline
    (a literal in a custom-SQL check). Neither belongs in a persisted, broadly
    readable field.

    What is deliberately KEPT is the driver's own first block. That message is the
    most actionable thing a user gets for a broken query ("Numeric value 'x' is not
    recognized", "Table does not exist"), and blanket-classifying it the way
    `failure_classifier` treats a connect failure would make a bad cast or a typo'd
    column undiagnosable from the UI — the same trade-off `SafeMonitorError`'s
    docstring records for `MonitorConfigError`. A warehouse message can quote the
    offending cell, and that is accepted here: it is the diagnostic, it is bounded
    to one value the driver chose to name, and removing it would leave the user
    with nothing. What this closes is the *bulk*, mechanical echo of the statement
    and every bound parameter, which is neither bounded nor diagnostic — the query
    is already visible to its author in the check editor.

    Idempotent, and a no-op on any message without the marker (a non-SQL engine's
    exception, a DataQ-authored message, ``None``), so it is safe to apply both
    where the message is persisted and where it is read back.
    """
    if not message:
        return message
    head, marker, _ = message.partition(_STATEMENT_ECHO_MARKER)
    return head.rstrip() if marker else message


def folding_identifier(name: str) -> Any:
    """Wrap ``name`` with an explicit quote decision: bare iff it is all lower-case.

    The #476 rule, made ours instead of SQLAlchemy's. Left to its defaults the
    compiler also quotes any name in the **dialect's reserved-word set**, which is
    not the same set the warehouse reserves — Snowflake does not reserve ``copy``,
    but SQLAlchemy's Snowflake dialect does, so a column stored ``COPY`` (created
    unquoted as ``copy``) would be emitted as ``"copy"`` and stop resolving. That
    is the very failure #476 exists to remove, reintroduced for one word.

    Pinning the decision explicitly makes the emitted form depend only on case:

    * **all lower-case → never quoted**, so the warehouse folds it exactly as it
      did before #476 (``order_ts`` → ``ORDER_TS``). This is what makes the change
      byte-for-byte behaviour-preserving rather than approximately so.
    * **anything else → always quoted**, which is the whole point: a mixed-case
      column is only reachable quoted.

    Genuinely reserved words (``order``, ``select``) are unreachable either way —
    bare is a parse error, and the folded object is ``ORDER``, which ``"order"``
    does not match. They were broken before this change and are broken after it,
    identically; alias them in a view.
    """
    from sqlalchemy.sql import quoted_name

    return quoted_name(name, quote=name != name.lower())


def _quote_namespace_part(name: str, dialect: Dialect) -> str:
    """Apply `folding_identifier`'s case-based decision to one namespace part
    that is about to be hand-assembled into a pre-quoted, dotted string (the
    3-part ``catalog.schema`` case — see `core_table`).

    A plain ``quoted_name`` can't be used here: Core's own quoting decision
    (`IdentifierPreparer.quote`) also fires on the dialect's *reserved-word*
    set, which is exactly what `folding_identifier` exists to bypass (#476).
    So the "should I quote" call is made here, case-only, same as
    `folding_identifier`; only the actual wrapping — the quote *character* —
    is delegated to the dialect, via ``identifier_preparer.quote_identifier``,
    which just wraps + escapes and makes no quoting decision of its own.
    """
    if name == name.lower():
        return name
    return str(dialect.identifier_preparer.quote_identifier(name))


def core_table(
    *,
    table: str,
    schema: str | None,
    catalog: str | None,
    dialect: Dialect | None = None,
) -> TableClause:
    """A Core table clause for ``[catalog.][schema.]table`` — the dialect quotes it.

    The one construction shared by the profiler's query builders and the monitor
    engine (#476). Going through Core rather than f-string interpolation is what
    makes a **mixed-case identifier** work at all, per `folding_identifier`'s rule.

    It must be Core and not hand-rolled quoting because the quote character is
    **dialect-specific** — Snowflake uses ``"``, Databricks/Unity Catalog uses
    backticks and reads ``"..."`` as a string literal — and this module is shared
    by both.

    **The 3-part (catalog) form needs a live ``dialect`` (#936).** Core's
    ``schema=`` slot is a single string, so a ``catalog.schema.table`` namespace
    has to be pre-assembled as one string for the dialect to emit dotted parts
    rather than quoting the whole thing as one identifier — and getting each part
    individually quote-correct then means making the "should I quote" decision
    ourselves (`_quote_namespace_part`, `folding_identifier`'s case rule applied
    per part) and, when a part needs quoting, wrapping it with the **dialect's
    own** ``identifier_preparer.quote_identifier`` rather than a hardcoded ``"``
    or backtick — so Snowflake and Unity Catalog each still get their own quote
    character despite the hand-assembly.

    All **three** parts go through the pre-assembly, not just catalog/schema —
    including the table, and via ``schema=None`` rather than Core's ``schema=``
    slot. Snowflake's own SQLAlchemy dialect turns out to already special-case a
    dotted *schema* string: ``quote_schema`` re-**splits** it back into parts and
    re-derives each part's quote decision from the whole string's single
    ``.quote`` flag, discarding any quote characters embedded in the parts
    themselves — so a schema-slot ``"MyCat"."Retail"`` (quote=False) round-trips
    back out as the *unquoted* ``MyCat.Retail``, silently undoing this fix on the
    one dialect it exists for. The **table**-name slot has no such override
    (``format_table``'s own name is quoted with the plain, non-splitting
    ``IdentifierPreparer.quote``), so folding the whole pre-quoted namespace in
    there — table included — and leaving ``schema=None`` sidesteps the
    reinterpretation entirely, on every dialect tested (Snowflake, Databricks,
    the SQLAlchemy default).

    A ``catalog`` with no ``dialect`` is a caller bug (every production caller has
    one available — the runner's engine, or the profiler/anomaly path's open
    connection) and is raised as `ValueError` rather than silently under-quoting
    again.

    That pre-quoted namespace is also the one raw interpolation left in the
    module, hence the allowlist check on every part here rather than trusting
    callers (they validate first for a good error message; this is the injection
    guarantee, and it survives a caller forgetting to validate).

    A ``catalog`` with no ``schema`` is refused: dropping the ``None`` schema would
    emit a 2-part ``catalog.table``, which Unity Catalog resolves as
    ``schema.table`` — a wrong object rather than an error.
    """
    from sqlalchemy import table as table_clause
    from sqlalchemy.sql import quoted_name

    if catalog is not None and schema is None:
        raise ValueError(f"table {table!r} has a catalog but no schema")
    for part, label in ((table, "table"), (schema, "schema"), (catalog, "catalog")):
        if part is not None and not is_sql_identifier(part):
            raise ValueError(f"invalid {label} identifier: {part!r}")

    if catalog is not None:
        if dialect is None:
            raise ValueError(f"table {table!r} has a catalog but no dialect to quote it")
        assert schema is not None  # guaranteed by the catalog/schema check above
        full = quoted_name(
            ".".join(_quote_namespace_part(part, dialect) for part in (catalog, schema, table)),
            quote=False,
        )
        return table_clause(full, schema=None)

    namespace: Any = None if schema is None else folding_identifier(schema)
    return table_clause(folding_identifier(table), schema=namespace)


def qualified_sql_name(
    *, table: str, schema: str | None, catalog: str | None, dialect: Dialect
) -> str:
    """``[catalog.][schema.]table`` as a pre-quoted string for a `text()` statement.

    `core_table` is the right tool wherever a Core `Select` can express the query;
    this exists for the one shape Core cannot render — a dialect-specific clause
    that attaches to the FROM item itself, like Databricks' ``TABLESAMPLE (x
    PERCENT)`` (#595). It reuses `_quote_namespace_part`, so each part gets
    `folding_identifier`'s case-only decision and, when it needs quoting, the
    **dialect's own** quote character (Snowflake ``"``, Databricks backticks) —
    never a hardcoded one, which is what made #476's hand-rolled quoting wrong on
    Unity Catalog.

    Every part is allowlist-checked here rather than trusted from the caller: this
    string is interpolated into SQL, so the injection guarantee has to survive a
    caller forgetting to validate first (the same reasoning `core_table` records).
    """
    if catalog is not None and schema is None:
        raise ValueError(f"table {table!r} has a catalog but no schema")
    parts = [(catalog, "catalog"), (schema, "schema"), (table, "table")]
    for part, label in parts:
        if part is not None and not is_sql_identifier(part):
            raise ValueError(f"invalid {label} identifier: {part!r}")
    return ".".join(_quote_namespace_part(part, dialect) for part, _ in parts if part is not None)


class LazyEngine:
    """One lazily-built SQLAlchemy engine with an idempotent dispose (#427).

    ``factory`` builds the engine on first :meth:`get` (the runner's URL /
    connect-args closure — the only per-datasource variance); every later call
    returns the same engine, so a runner's SQL touchpoints share one pool and
    one auth handshake per run. :meth:`close` disposes the pool and resets, so
    a closed holder lazily rebuilds if reused — never a bricked runner.
    """

    def __init__(self, factory: Callable[[], Any]) -> None:
        self._factory = factory
        self._engine: Any | None = None

    def get(self) -> Any:
        if self._engine is None:
            self._engine = self._factory()
        return self._engine

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self._engine is not None:
            self._engine.dispose()
            self._engine = None

from pydantic import Field, ValidationInfo, field_validator, model_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

# Migration message for the secret store ADR 0039 removed. Lives here (not in
# `secrets.py`, which imports this module) so the startup validator and the
# `_build_store` fallback cannot drift apart.
_REDIS_STORE_REMOVED: Final = (
    "SECRET_STORE='redis' was removed in ADR 0039 — the store kept credentials in "
    "plaintext. Use SECRET_STORE=openbao (set OPENBAO_ADDR + OPENBAO_TOKEN; "
    "`docker compose up` starts the vault) and re-enter connection credentials. "
    "Then PURGE the old plaintext values, which outlive the switch: "
    "redis-cli --scan --pattern 'dataq:secret:*' | xargs -r redis-cli del. See "
    "docs/site/adr/0039-openbao-self-hosted-secret-backend.md"
)

# OTP-mailer transport defaults. Named constants (not inline literals) because
# `_blank_email_transport_means_default` has to hand back the same values a blank
# env var should fall through to — two copies of "587" would drift.
AuthEmailTlsMode = Literal["starttls", "implicit", "none"]
_DEFAULT_AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_PORT: Final = 587
_DEFAULT_AUTH_EMAIL_TLS_MODE: Final[AuthEmailTlsMode] = "starttls"
_AUTH_EMAIL_TRANSPORT_DEFAULTS: Final[dict[str, object]] = {
    "auth_email_smtp_port": _DEFAULT_AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_PORT,
    "auth_email_tls_mode": _DEFAULT_AUTH_EMAIL_TLS_MODE,
}

# Default MCP transport Host allowlist: the Azure Container Apps internal-ingress
# FQDN shape the frontend nginx proxies to, plus the compose service name and
# loopback. Overridable via MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS for any other deploy target (#728).
_MCP_DEFAULT_ALLOWED_HOSTS = ("*.azurecontainerapps.io", "api", "localhost", "127.0.0.1")


def _allowed_email_set(raw: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Parse a comma-separated signup allowlist into normalized addresses.

    Normalization is strip + lower — the SAME rule as `Settings.is_admin_email`,
    `otp_service.normalize_email` and the `uq_users_email_lower` index. The
    identity surface has exactly one rule (ADR 0032 decision 6), so both the OTP
    and the generic-OIDC allowlists (#1386) go through this one function rather
    than each spelling it out.
    """
    return frozenset(part.strip().lower() for part in raw.split(",") if part.strip())


def _allowed_domain_set(raw: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Parse a comma-separated signup allowlist into normalized domains.

    A leading `@` is tolerated and stripped, because `@acme.io` is what an
    operator naturally writes and a silently-never-matching allowlist is a
    fail-OPEN-*looking* config error: every address reads as ineligible and the
    uniform response hides which half is wrong.
    """
    return frozenset(
        part.strip().lower().lstrip("@") for part in raw.split(",") if part.strip().lstrip("@")
    )


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        # App config lives in .env.app (host dev reads it directly; compose injects
        # it into the api/worker containers via env_file). The root .env is
        # compose/infra-only (POSTGRES_*, VITE_*) and is NOT read here. extra=forbid
        # catches typo'd/stale keys — the split keeps those infra keys from tripping
        # it. See #209.
        env_file=".env.app",
        env_file_encoding="utf-8",
        extra="forbid",
        case_sensitive=False,
    )

    environment: Literal["dev", "staging", "prod"] = "dev"
    log_level: Literal["DEBUG", "INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR", "CRITICAL"] = "INFO"

    # No DB credentials embedded in code. The real URL (with password) comes from
    # the environment: docker-compose and CI set DATABASE_URL; local host dev gets
    # it from .env (setup.sh bootstraps + exports it). This default is only a
    # credential-less placeholder for the no-env case.
    database_url: str = Field(default="postgresql+psycopg2://localhost:5432/dataq")
    redis_url: str = Field(default="redis://localhost:6379/0")

    applicationinsights_connection_string: str | None = None

    # Generic OTLP/HTTP exporter endpoint (#589) — the standard OTel contract
    # (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT). When set, spans AND logs also export to this
    # OTLP consumer (Grafana/Tempo, Jaeger, Datadog, …) via the OTLP/HTTP exporter,
    # with base-endpoint semantics (`/v1/traces` + `/v1/logs` appended). The Azure

    # HTTP receiver (Marquez, an OpenLineage collector, …). Typed here — not read
    # from raw os.environ — so a value in `.env.app` (which the process env never
    # sees) still activates emission. The library-owned advanced transports

1	"""GX-agnostic run core: drive the `Run` lifecycle via an injected `CheckRunner`.
2	
3	Run.status describes *execution*, not data quality: a completed run is
4	``succeeded`` even when checks fail; ``failed`` means the adapter could not execute.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import uuid
10	from collections import defaultdict
11	from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator, Mapping, Sequence
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
14	from typing import Any, Literal, cast
15	
16	from sqlalchemy import delete, func, null, select, update
17	from sqlalchemy.engine import CursorResult
18	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
19	
20	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError

22	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
23	from backend.app.core.timeutil import as_utc
24	from backend.app.datasources.base import (
25	    SAMPLE_ROW_CAP,
26	    VALUE_SIGNAL_SUMMARY_KEY,
27	    CheckOutcome,
28	    CheckRunner,
29	    CheckSpec,
30	    MonitorRunner,
31	    MonitorSpec,
32	)
33	from backend.app.datasources.monitors import (
34	    MONITOR_KINDS,
35	    SCALAR_MONITOR_KINDS,
36	    STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS,
37	)
38	from backend.app.datasources.sql import strip_statement_echo
39	from backend.app.db.chunked_dml import CHUNK_SIZE, chunked_dml
40	from backend.app.db.models import (
41	    CHECK_ORDER,
42	    COMPARISON_KIND,
43	    GX_ENGINE,
44	    RESULT_OPERATIONAL_STATUSES,
45	    RESULT_STATUSES,
46	    RUN_STATUSES,
47	    SEVERITY_RANK,
48	    Asset,
49	    Check,
50	    CheckVersion,
51	    Result,
52	    Run,
53	    worst_severity,
54	)
55	from backend.app.services import run_dispatch, suite_service
56	from backend.app.services.column_classification import ColumnClass, classify_column, is_sensitive
57	from backend.app.services.failure_classifier import safe_failure_reason
58	from backend.app.services.rollup import status_histograms
59	from backend.app.services.severity import resolve_status
60	
61	log = get_logger(__name__)
62	
63	
64	def _now() -> datetime:
65	    return datetime.now(UTC)
66	
67	
68	def _build_result(run_id: uuid.UUID, check: Check, outcome: CheckOutcome) -> Result:
69	    """Map a check + its GX outcome to a `Result`, deriving the severity tier
70	    (ADR 0005/0016; the scalar persists as `metric_value`, ADR 0012).
71	
72	    An errored check (#122) is an operational ``error``, never banded `fail`; its
73	    message passes `strip_statement_echo` (#1203) because a SQL engine's
74	    `[SQL: …] [parameters: …]` tail echoes target data into a field outside the
75	    column-policy path.
76	    """
77	    status, metric = resolve_status(
78	        outcome,
79	        warn_threshold=check.warn_threshold,
80	        fail_threshold=check.fail_threshold,
81	        critical_threshold=check.critical_threshold,
82	    )
83	    if outcome.errored:
84	        # The one funnel to `observed_value` for every kind/datasource, so the
85	        # #1203 strip cannot diverge per runner.
86	        error_message = strip_statement_echo(outcome.error_message)
87	        observed = {"error": error_message} if error_message else None
88	        # The provoking target cell (#989) rides separately from the message so
89	        # the read layer can redact it under the suite's column policy.
90	        if outcome.observed_value and "unparsed_value" in outcome.observed_value:
91	            observed = {**(observed or {}), **sanitize_json(outcome.observed_value)}
92	        sample = None
93	    else:
94	        observed = sanitize_json(outcome.observed_value)
95	        sample = sanitize_json(outcome.sample_failures)
96	    return Result(
97	        run_id=run_id,
98	        check_id=check.id,
99	        status=status,
100	        metric_value=metric,
101	        observed_value=observed,
102	        expected_value=sanitize_json(outcome.expected_value),
103	        sample_failures=sample,
104	        # Persisted on EVERY status, incl. `error` (#595) — "this run was reading
105	        # a sample" is still true of the read that failed.
106	        sampling=sanitize_json(outcome.sampling),
107	    )
108	
109	
110	_EXPECTATION_KIND = "expectation"
111	
112	
113	@dataclass(frozen=True)
114	class OutcomePhase:
115	    """One unit of execution: ``(check index, outcome)`` pairs plus whether the
116	    phase's rows may be committed as soon as built (#318) — see
117	    `_run_outcome_phases` for the publishability rule."""
118	
119	    resolved: list[tuple[int, CheckOutcome]]
120	    publishable: bool
121	
122	
123	def _run_outcome_phases(
124	    runner: CheckRunner,
125	    *,
126	    table: str,
127	    schema: str | None,
128	    checks: list[Check],
129	    index_columns: list[str] | None = None,
130	    comparison_executor: Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome] | None = None,
131	    stateful_monitor_executor: Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome] | None = None,
132	) -> Iterator[OutcomePhase]:
133	    """Run a suite's checks, dispatched by `check.kind` (ADR 0012), yielding each
134	    unit of execution as it resolves.
135	
136	    Phase granularity is the ENGINE's property, not a choice: each comparison or
137	    native-engine check is its own phase; all GX expectations are ONE atomic batch;
138	    scalar monitors share one loaded frame. Stateful kinds (``schema_drift``/
139	    ``anomaly``) are yielded LAST and unpublishable: their executors write
140	    ``monitor_baselines`` through the caller's session, and committing early would
141	    make a failed run's baseline durable — poisoning the anomaly window and the
142	    drift reference for every later run (#318). A missing injected executor yields
143	    a per-check operational ``error`` (#122); a kind with no run path raises.
144	    """
145	
146	    # Engine partition first (ADR 0036): a native check routes to the runner's
147	    # `run_native_check` when advertised (`supported_native_engines`, #429), else
148	    # lands as a classified per-check `error` — never a silent skip, never a raise
149	    # that takes the GX siblings down (§5). Connection-establishment failures still
150	    # propagate: an unreachable warehouse fails the whole run operationally.
151	    # A transient (unflushed) check has no server-default yet → None means 'gx'.
152	    def _engine(c: Check) -> str:
153	        return c.engine or GX_ENGINE
154	
155	    advertised = frozenset(getattr(runner, "supported_native_engines", frozenset()))
156	    native_run = getattr(runner, "run_native_check", None)
157	    for i, c in enumerate(checks):
158	        engine = _engine(c)
159	        if engine == GX_ENGINE:
160	            continue
161	        if engine in advertised and callable(native_run):
162	            outcome = cast(
163	                CheckOutcome,
164	                native_run(
165	                    kind=c.kind,
166	                    expectation_type=c.expectation_type,
167	                    config=dict(c.config),
168	                    table=table,
169	                    schema=schema,
170	                ),
171	            )
172	        else:
173	            outcome = _executor_outcome(
174	                None,
175	                c,
176	                missing=(
177	                    f"engine '{engine}' is not available on this "
178	                    "connection — the check was authored for a "
179	                    "platform-native engine this deployment cannot run "
180	                    "(ADR 0036); re-check the connection's engine "
181	                    "capabilities or re-point the check to 'gx'"
182	                ),
183	            )
184	        yield OutcomePhase(resolved=[(i, outcome)], publishable=True)
185	    checks_gx = [(i, c) for i, c in enumerate(checks) if _engine(c) == GX_ENGINE]
186	    expectation_idx = [i for i, c in checks_gx if c.kind == _EXPECTATION_KIND]
187	    monitor_idx = [i for i, c in checks_gx if c.kind in SCALAR_MONITOR_KINDS]
188	    stateful_idx = [i for i, c in checks_gx if c.kind in STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS]
189	    comparison_idx = [i for i, c in checks_gx if c.kind == COMPARISON_KIND]
190	    handled = {_EXPECTATION_KIND, *MONITOR_KINDS, COMPARISON_KIND}
191	    # GX partition only: a native-engine check was already resolved above —
192	    # raising here would resolve it twice and take its GX siblings down.
193	    unsupported = sorted({c.kind for _, c in checks_gx if c.kind not in handled})
194	    if unsupported:
195	        raise NotImplementedError(f"no run path for check kind(s) {', '.join(unsupported)}")
196	
197	    # Comparison is read-only, so it publishes; stateful writes baselines, so it
198	    # does not — and is deliberately yielded LAST (see docstring).
199	    for i in comparison_idx:
200	        yield OutcomePhase(
201	            resolved=[
202	                (
203	                    i,
204	                    _executor_outcome(
205	                        comparison_executor,
206	                        checks[i],
207	                        missing=(
208	                            "comparison checks need the comparison run path (no executor "
209	                            "supplied on this caller — ADR 0015)"
210	                        ),
211	                    ),
212	                )
213	            ],
214	            publishable=True,
215	        )
216	    if expectation_idx:
217	        specs = [
218	            CheckSpec(expectation_type=checks[i].expectation_type, kwargs=dict(checks[i].config))
219	            for i in expectation_idx
220	        ]
221	        suite_outcome = runner.run_checks(
222	            table=table, schema=schema, checks=specs, index_columns=index_columns
223	        )
224	        # One phase: GX resolved them in a single atomic batch. `strict=True`
225	        # keeps a wrong-arity runner loud.
226	        yield OutcomePhase(
227	            resolved=list(zip(expectation_idx, suite_outcome.checks, strict=True)),
228	            publishable=True,
229	        )
230	    if monitor_idx:
231	        # Capability gate (#429): never `isinstance(runner, MonitorRunner)` — a
232	        # runtime_checkable Protocol matches on method NAME alone and would
233	        # TypeError at the call.
234	        supported = frozenset(getattr(runner, "supported_monitor_kinds", frozenset()))
235	        unsupported_kinds = sorted({checks[i].kind for i in monitor_idx} - supported)
236	        if unsupported_kinds:
237	            raise NotImplementedError(
238	                f"{type(runner).__name__} does not support monitor kind(s) "
239	                f"{', '.join(unsupported_kinds)} — these need a monitor-capable "
240	                "datasource (Snowflake / Unity Catalog / Iceberg / ADLS Gen2 / S3)"
241	            )
242	        if not callable(getattr(runner, "run_monitors", None)):
243	            # Advertising kinds without the method must reject as cleanly as the reverse.
244	            raise NotImplementedError(
245	                f"{type(runner).__name__} advertises monitor kinds but implements "
246	                "no run_monitors — runner capability and implementation drifted"
247	            )
248	        monitor_runner = cast(MonitorRunner, runner)
249	        monitors = [
250	            MonitorSpec(kind=checks[i].kind, config=dict(checks[i].config)) for i in monitor_idx
251	        ]
252	        monitor_outcomes = monitor_runner.run_monitors(
253	            table=table, schema=schema, monitors=monitors
254	        )
255	        # One phase: `run_monitors` loads the frame once for the whole list.
256	        yield OutcomePhase(
257	            resolved=list(zip(monitor_idx, monitor_outcomes, strict=True)),
258	            publishable=True,
259	        )
260	    # LAST and unpublishable: these write `monitor_baselines` through the caller's
261	    # session, so their rows must ride the terminal commit (see docstring).
262	    for i in stateful_idx:
263	        yield OutcomePhase(
264	            resolved=[
265	                (
266	                    i,
267	                    _executor_outcome(
268	                        stateful_monitor_executor,
269	                        checks[i],
270	                        missing=(
271	                            "stateful monitor kinds need the baseline-diff run path (no "
272	                            "executor supplied on this caller — #592)"
273	                        ),
274	                    ),
275	                )
276	            ],
277	            publishable=False,
278	        )
279	
280	
281	def _executor_outcome(
282	    executor: Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome] | None,
283	    check: Check,
284	    *,
285	    missing: str,
286	) -> CheckOutcome:
287	    """Run an injected per-check executor, or report its absence as an operational
288	    ``error`` (#122) — never a raise, so siblings still run."""
289	    if executor is None:
290	        return CheckOutcome(
291	            expectation_type=check.expectation_type,
292	            success=False,
293	            errored=True,
294	            error_message=missing,
295	        )
296	    return executor(check)
297	
298	
299	def _cancelled_mid_run(session: Session, run: Run) -> bool:
300	    """Did a cancel commit (from the API session) while this run was executing?
301	
302	    A scalar column read, not ``session.refresh(run)``: avoids a per-phase full
303	    ORM re-load and structurally cannot flush the caller's staged rows.
304	    """
305	    if session.scalar(select(Run.status).where(Run.id == run.id)) != "cancelled":
306	        return False
307	    # Sync the ORM object only on the rare cancelled path — callers read `run.status`.
308	    session.refresh(run)
309	    return True
310	
311	
312	def discard_run_results(session: Session, run_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
313	    """Drop every result row a run wrote — staged AND committed (#318).
314	
315	    Hygiene, NOT the safety net: aggregate readers already exclude non-succeeded
316	    runs (`rollup.AGGREGATABLE_RUN_STATUSES`) — a compensating DELETE that can
317	    itself fail is a poor place for an invariant. Best-effort: if it fails, the
318	    caller must still record the terminal status (a stuck ``running`` run is the
319	    worse outcome).
320	    """
321	    session.rollback()
322	    try:
323	        session.execute(delete(Result).where(Result.run_id == run_id))
324	        session.commit()
325	    except Exception:
326	        session.rollback()
327	        log.exception("run_partial_results_discard_failed", run_id=str(run_id))
328	
329	
330	def execute_run(
331	    session: Session,
332	    *,
333	    run: Run,
334	    checks: list[Check],
335	    runner: CheckRunner,
336	    table: str,
337	    schema: str | None = None,
338	    index_columns: list[str] | None = None,
339	    comparison_executor: Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome] | None = None,
340	    stateful_monitor_executor: Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome] | None = None,
341	) -> Run:
342	    """Run ``checks`` against ``table`` via ``runner`` and persist the outcome.
343	
344	    ``run`` must already be persisted. Publishable results commit per execution
345	    phase (#318); stateful monitor phases ride the terminal commit (see
346	    `_run_outcome_phases`). Terminal contract: a run that ends ``failed``/
347	    ``cancelled`` has NO result rows.
348	    """
349	    run.status = "running"
350	    run.started_at = _now()
351	    session.commit()
352	    log.info(
353	        "run_started",
354	        run_id=str(run.id),
355	        suite_id=str(run.suite_id),
356	        n_checks=len(checks),
357	        table=table,
358	    )
359	
360	    # Everything below is guarded so any failure drives the run terminal-'failed'
361	    # rather than stuck 'running'. Only a boolean + count cross phases, never the
362	    # CheckOutcomes: retaining failing-row samples for one log line is the worker
363	    # memory #595 guards against.
364	    suite_success = True
365	    n_results = 0
366	    published = False
367	    try:
368	        for phase in _run_outcome_phases(
369	            runner,
370	            table=table,
371	            schema=schema,
372	            checks=checks,
373	            index_columns=index_columns,
374	            comparison_executor=comparison_executor,
375	            stateful_monitor_executor=stateful_monitor_executor,
376	        ):
377	            rows = [
378	                _build_result(run.id, checks[i], check_outcome)
379	                for i, check_outcome in phase.resolved
380	            ]
381	            session.add_all(rows)
382	            suite_success = suite_success and all(oc.success for _, oc in phase.resolved)
383	            n_results += len(rows)
384	            # Cooperative cancellation before every commit: a committed cancel must
385	            # not be overwritten — drop staged + committed rows, leave 'cancelled'.
386	            if _cancelled_mid_run(session, run):
387	                _discard_results_if_any(session, run, published=published)
388	                log.info("run_cancelled_during_execution", run_id=str(run.id))
389	                return run
390	            if not phase.publishable:
391	                # Rows ride the terminal commit with the phase's `monitor_baselines`
392	                # writes (#318 G1) — committing here would make those durable early.
393	                continue
394	            # The commit that makes this phase visible to the progress poll.
395	            session.commit()
396	            published = True
397	        # A cancel can still land between the last commit and the terminal flip
398	        # (two transactions); the flip below guards the remaining window itself.
399	        if _cancelled_mid_run(session, run):
400	            _discard_results_if_any(session, run, published=published)
401	            log.info("run_cancelled_during_execution", run_id=str(run.id))
402	            return run
403	        if not _mark_succeeded(session, run):
404	            # Lost the race: the conditional WHERE keeps the user's confirmed
405	            # cancel authoritative instead of silently overwritten (#318 G4).
406	            _discard_results_if_any(session, run, published=published)
407	            session.refresh(run)
408	            log.info("run_cancelled_during_execution", run_id=str(run.id))
409	            return run
410	    except Exception as exc:
411	        _discard_results_if_any(session, run, published=published)
412	        # A cancelled run that also errored stays 'cancelled', not masked as 'failed'.
413	        if _cancelled_mid_run(session, run):
414	            log.info("run_cancelled_during_execution", run_id=str(run.id))
415	            return run
416	        run.status = "failed"
417	        run.finished_at = _now()
418	        # Redaction-safe reason (#605/#595): raw text can carry DSN/credential/cell
419	        # fragments — it stays in the server log, never the persisted reason.
420	        # Shared with the monitor loop and dry-run so the three sinks cannot drift.
421	        run.failure_reason = safe_failure_reason(exc)
422	        session.commit()
423	        log.exception("run_failed", run_id=str(run.id), table=table)
424	        return run
425	
426	    log.info(
427	        "run_completed",
428	        run_id=str(run.id),
429	        suite_success=suite_success,
430	        n_results=n_results,
431	    )
432	    return run
433	
434	
435	def _mark_succeeded(session: Session, run: Run) -> bool:
436	    """Flip a still-``running`` run to ``succeeded``; return whether it won (#318 G4).
437	
438	    A conditional ``UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'running'`` rather than an ORM
439	    attribute set, so a cancel that commits between the last `_cancelled_mid_run`
440	    check and this statement loses instead of being silently overwritten. The
441	    check-then-set shape cannot close that window at any distance — only the
442	    predicate travelling with the write can — and the run's own docstring states
443	    the terminal contract absolutely, so the window has to be closed rather than
444	    narrowed.
445	
446	    ``failure_reason`` is cleared in the same statement: a slow-but-alive worker
447	    whose run was already reaped (failed + REAPED_REASON) can still finish and win
448	    here, and must not surface as succeeded-with-a-failure-reason (#605).
449	    """
450	    finished = _now()
451	    result = session.execute(
452	        update(Run)
453	        .where(Run.id == run.id, Run.status == "running")
454	        .values(status="succeeded", finished_at=finished, failure_reason=None)
455	    )
456	    # `rowcount` is on `CursorResult`, which is what a DML `execute` always
457	    # returns; the declared `Result` supertype does not carry it.
458	    won = cast("CursorResult[Any]", result).rowcount == 1
459	    session.commit()
460	    if not won:
461	        return False
462	    # Mirror the write onto the in-memory object: the Core UPDATE bypassed the
463	    # ORM and callers read `run.status` straight after this returns. These are the
464	    # values we just wrote, so the two cannot diverge, and it saves the re-SELECT
465	    # a `refresh` would cost on the hot path.
466	    run.status = "succeeded"
467	    run.finished_at = finished
468	    run.failure_reason = None
469	    return True
470	
471	
472	def _discard_results_if_any(session: Session, run: Run, *, published: bool) -> None:
473	    """`discard_run_results`, skipped when no phase ever committed.
474	
475	    The common failure — an expectation-only suite whose GX batch raises — has
476	    published nothing, so the staged rows die with the rollback and a DELETE +
477	    COMMIT round trip would be pure overhead on the path that is already
478	    handling an error.
479	    """
480	    if published:
481	        discard_run_results(session, run.id)
482	    else:
483	        session.rollback()
484	
485	
486	def skip_run(session: Session, *, run: Run, checks: list[Check], reason: str) -> Run:
487	    """Record a run that had nothing to evaluate — every check `skip`ped (#122).
488	
489	    Used when the adapter is never invoked because there's no data to validate
490	    (e.g. the target batch hasn't landed yet). The run still **succeeds** — it
491	    executed end to end, it just found nothing to check — and each check gets a
492	    ``skip`` Result carrying the ``reason`` (operational, not a severity tier, so
493	    it's excluded from the health-score N per ADR 0005). Distinct from ``failed``,
494	    which means the run could not execute.
495	    """
496	    run.status = "running"
497	    run.started_at = _now()
498	    session.commit()
499	    rows = [
500	        Result(run_id=run.id, check_id=check.id, status="skip", observed_value={"reason": reason})
501	        for check in checks
502	    ]
503	    session.add_all(rows)
504	    run.status = "succeeded"
505	    run.finished_at = _now()
506	    session.commit()
507	    log.info("run_skipped", run_id=str(run.id), reason=reason, n_checks=len(checks))
508	    return run
509	
510	
511	# ── read model (PR-C0b: the runs/results surface) ────────────────────────────
512	# Reads are scoped to suites the user can access — owned (`created_by`) or shared
513	# (`shares`), the same visibility `suite_service.list_suites` enforces. The API
514	# layer additionally calls `require_permission` for single-suite / single-run
515	# lookups (404 hides existence); this subquery is the defence-in-depth filter so
516	# a list query can never leak a run from a suite the caller can't see.
517	
518	
519	class RunFilterInvalidError(DataQError):
520	    status_code = 422
521	    code = "run_filter_invalid"
522	
523	
524	def validate_read_filters(status: str | None = None) -> None:
525	    """422 on a `/runs` filter value outside its closed vocabulary.
526	
527	    Mirrors `orchestration_service.validate_read_filters` (#306) and the
528	    `/incidents` `state` gate: an unrecognised ``status`` used to flow straight
529	    into the `WHERE`, so `?status=succeded` (or the wrong-case `Succeeded` —
530	    the column stores lower-case) answered `200 []` with `X-Total-Count: 0`,
531	    indistinguishable from "no runs are in that status". That is the
532	    confidently-empty-answer class (#828) this codebase guards everywhere else.
533	    ``None`` means "no filter" and is left alone; only a *supplied* value is
534	    checked.
535	    """
536	    if status is not None and status not in RUN_STATUSES:
537	        raise RunFilterInvalidError(
538	            f"invalid run status {status!r}", detail={"allowed": list(RUN_STATUSES)}
539	        )
540	
541	
542	def _run_filters(
543	    *,
544	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
545	    suite_id: uuid.UUID | None,
546	    status: str | None,
547	    include_all: bool,
548	) -> list[Any]:
549	    """The ONE `WHERE` chain shared by :func:`list_runs` and :func:`count_runs`.
550	
551	    Derived once rather than hand-rolled twice, so a future filter cannot land on
552	    the list without the total — which would make `X-Total-Count` quietly
553	    disagree with the page it describes (#1108)."""
554	    conditions: list[Any] = [
555	        Run.suite_id.in_(suite_service.accessible_suite_ids(user_id, include_all=include_all))
556	    ]
557	    if suite_id is not None:
558	        conditions.append(Run.suite_id == suite_id)
559	    if status is not None:
560	        conditions.append(Run.status == status)
561	    return conditions
562	
563	
564	def list_runs(
565	    session: Session,
566	    *,
567	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
568	    suite_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
569	    status: str | None = None,
570	    limit: int = 50,
571	    offset: int = 0,
572	    include_all: bool = False,
573	) -> list[Run]:
574	    """Runs for suites the user can access, newest first (`created_at` desc,
575	    `id` desc tie-break — the same total-order paging shape `/pipeline_runs`
576	    and `/incidents` use, since `created_at` alone ties within one transaction).
577	
578	    Optionally narrowed to one ``suite_id`` and/or a ``status``. The accessible
579	    subquery is always applied, so passing a ``suite_id`` the user can't see
580	    yields an empty list (the API layer 404s that case up front via
581	    `require_permission`, but the filter keeps the service safe on its own).
582	    ``include_all`` spans every suite — the workspace-admin view (ADR 0027).
583	    """
584	    stmt = (
585	        select(Run)
586	        .where(
587	            *_run_filters(
588	                user_id=user_id, suite_id=suite_id, status=status, include_all=include_all
589	            )
590	        )
591	        .order_by(Run.created_at.desc(), Run.id.desc())
592	        .limit(limit)
593	        .offset(offset)
594	    )
595	    return list(session.scalars(stmt))
596	
597	
598	def count_runs(
599	    session: Session,
600	    *,
601	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
602	    suite_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
603	    status: str | None = None,
604	    include_all: bool = False,
605	) -> int:
606	    """Total runs matching the SAME visibility + filters as :func:`list_runs`,
607	    unaffected by its `limit`/`offset` (#1108 — the `/assets` `X-Total-Count`
608	    shape: `/runs` had `limit` only and could not be paged at all). Shares
609	    :func:`_run_filters` with the list so the two cannot drift."""
610	    stmt = (
611	        select(func.count())
612	        .select_from(Run)
613	        .where(
614	            *_run_filters(
615	                user_id=user_id, suite_id=suite_id, status=status, include_all=include_all
616	            )
617	        )
618	    )
619	    return session.scalar(stmt) or 0
620	
621	
622	def check_outcome_counts(
623	    session: Session,
624	    run_ids: Sequence[uuid.UUID],
625	    *,
626	    complete_runs_only: bool = False,
627	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, tuple[int, int, str | None]]:
628	    """Per-run ``(checks_total, checks_passed, worst_severity)`` for a set of runs,
629	    in a single grouped query (no N+1). ``worst_severity`` is the highest of
630	    warn/fail/critical present, else ``None`` (all passed / only operational).
631	
632	    ``complete_runs_only`` forwards to `rollup.status_histograms` and is for
633	    callers presenting these numbers as a **suite's** standing rather than as one
634	    named run's outcome — the asset view passes it, the runs table does not (a
635	    live run legitimately reads ``3 / 7`` there).
636	
637	    ``checks_total``/``checks_passed`` count **evaluated** checks — the four
638	    severity tiers (pass/warn/fail/critical) — and **exclude** operational
639	    ``skip``/``error`` (#122), so the X/Y matches the run-detail page's "Checks
640	    passed" denominator and an all-skip run reports total 0 (rendered ``—``, not a
641	    misleading green ``0/N``).
642	
643	    Lets the runs list surface a run's *data-quality* outcome — distinct from the
644	    run's *execution* status, which is ``succeeded`` even when checks failed."""
645	    out: dict[uuid.UUID, tuple[int, int, str | None]] = {}
646	    # A fold over the ONE shared histogram query (#889) — this used to build the
647	    # same `{status: count}` mapping itself and then discard it, which is exactly
648	    # the shape the health score needs.
649	    for run_id, by_status in status_histograms(
650	        session, run_ids, complete_runs_only=complete_runs_only
651	    ).items():
652	        passed = by_status.get("pass", 0)
653	        # Worst check outcome via the single shared severity helper (#655); skip/error
654	        # aren't failing tiers, so they never rank.
655	        worst = worst_severity(by_status)
656	        # Evaluated checks only: pass + the three failing tiers (skip/error excluded).
657	        total = passed + sum(by_status.get(tier, 0) for tier in SEVERITY_RANK)
658	        out[run_id] = (total, passed, worst)
659	    return out
660	
661	
662	def operational_result_flags(
663	    session: Session, run_ids: Sequence[uuid.UUID]
664	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, tuple[bool, bool]]:
665	    """Per-run ``(has_error, has_skip)`` over its **operational** results (#122).
666	
667	    The exact complement of :func:`check_outcome_counts`, which counts only the
668	    *evaluated* severity tiers and deliberately drops ``skip``/``error``. Those
669	    dropped rows are the signal that DataQ could not evaluate a check — the
670	    datasource threw (``error``) or a precondition wasn't met (``skip``) — so the
671	    asset view reads them to derive **connection** health (can we reach the thing?)
672	    separately from **suite** health (is the data good?), per #803.
673	
674	    Presence, not counts: one grouped query, a row exists iff that status occurs.
675	    """
676	    if not run_ids:
677	        return {}
678	    rows = session.execute(
679	        select(Result.run_id, Result.status)
680	        .where(Result.run_id.in_(run_ids), Result.status.in_(RESULT_OPERATIONAL_STATUSES))
681	        .group_by(Result.run_id, Result.status)
682	    ).all()
683	    flags: dict[uuid.UUID, tuple[bool, bool]] = {}
684	    for run_id, status in rows:
685	        has_error, has_skip = flags.get(run_id, (False, False))
686	        flags[run_id] = (has_error or status == "error", has_skip or status == "skip")
687	    return flags
688	
689	
690	def get_run(session: Session, run_id: uuid.UUID) -> Run | None:
691	    """Fetch a run by id (no authz — the API layer gates on the run's suite)."""
692	    return session.get(Run, run_id)
693	
694	
695	_TERMINAL_STATUSES = frozenset({"succeeded", "failed", "cancelled"})
696	# The complement, single-sourced from the canonical status set so a new
697	# lifecycle status can't silently escape the reaper's net (#309).
698	_NON_TERMINAL_STATUSES = frozenset(RUN_STATUSES) - _TERMINAL_STATUSES
